turns.content: How does Naive Bayes classify a new email? I think it finds P(spam) and then P(spam|free).
Good start, but the second part is flipped. Naive Bayes estimates P(feature|class), such as P(free|spam), combines those likelihoods with the prior P(class), and compares the class scores.
So for each class I multiply the prior by the feature likelihoods?
Exactly. You compute a score for each class using the prior and conditional feature probabilities, then pick the highest scoring class.
What happens if one feature never appeared with a class in training?
That is the zero-frequency problem. Without smoothing, one zero conditional probability can make the whole product zero, so Laplace smoothing is used to avoid that.
